quest.title: The Realm of People
quest.description: The Lantern Rite is here. What new changes await in Liyue Harbor this year?
quest.rewards_formatted: Adventure EXP x450, Mora x44000, Hero's Wit x5, Mystic Enhancement Ore x10

chapter.num: A Lanternlit Ode to the Silver Moon: Act III
chapter.title: The Realm of People

talks.objective: Wait until 08:00 two days from now

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Xiao, Cloud Retainer, Madame Ping! We're here! Any news on Zhongli?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wait, aren't we missing two adepti?

dialogues.speaker: Madame Ping
dialogues.text: Hehe, well, Xianyun banned Mountain Shaper from Mt. Aocang for three days.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh... Then what about Moon Carver?

dialogues.speaker: Xianyun
dialogues.text: *scoff* The scheme to plant mint in one's abode was one those two fools devised together! And when it comes to punishment, one does not discriminate. His banishment ends in three days as well.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wow, that's pretty harsh, Cloud Retainer!

dialogues.speaker: Xiao
dialogues.text: Let's get down to business. We have news of Rex Lapis.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh? Isn't that...?

dialogues.speaker: Xianyun
dialogues.text: Yes, Rex Lapis' Geo pillar. It descended from on high this morning. He must have sent it for a reason, but it does not respond to our touch...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: So, what does it mean? Is he in trouble?

dialogues.speaker: Xiao
dialogues.text: Not necessarily. It could be a message only a specific person is meant to receive.

dialogues.speaker: Xiao
dialogues.text: #{NICKNAME}, you alone spoke to Rex Lapis before he left.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #Oh! So, it must be for {NICKNAME}!

dialogues.speaker: Xiao
dialogues.text: Give it a try.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (Touch the pillar.)

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: As you feel solid rock beneath your fingers, a familiar voice rings through your mind...

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: "Come to the spring on Mt. Qingce. I have left an entrance for you..."

dialogues.speaker: Xiao
dialogues.text: Well?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Seems like he might be over at Mt. Qingce.

dialogues.speaker: Xianyun
dialogues.text: Just as one surmised. It seems that Rex Lapis will not countenance our involvement in this matter.

dialogues.speaker: Madame Ping
dialogues.text: #Heh, that would not surprise me in the slightest. He's always had a soft spot for {NICKNAME}, after all.

dialogues.speaker: Madame Ping
dialogues.text: But be that as it may, we have served Rex Lapis for millennia now. In other words, I'm sure this has nothing to do with favoritism — he's probably just trying to protect us.

dialogues.speaker: Xiao
dialogues.text: That's right. So you mustn't let your guard down, even if Rex Lapis is by your side.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Don't worry, I won't.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Alright, let's get going. We'll try not to keep you all waiting!
Who could have imagined that the once mighty Geo Archon might end up so? Sitting on a humble stool in the woods, quietly weaving Moon Lanterns...
You really do look like an old man now.

dialogues.speaker: Zhongli
dialogues.text: This is a Xiao Lantern, not a Moon Lantern.
Hmm?

dialogues.speaker: Zhongli
dialogues.text: In ages past, when the gods waged war and the world was in turmoil, these lanterns were lit to guide fallen warriors back to their homes.

dialogues.speaker: Zhongli
dialogues.text: Had you tarried in the mortal realm for but a little while longer, you might have become quite accustomed to them.
Even so, it bears such a striking resemblance to the Moon Lanterns they used to offer up to the heavens. Could this truly be mere coincidence?

dialogues.speaker: Zhongli
dialogues.text: Perhaps in some sense it is, yet in another, it isn't.

dialogues.speaker: Zhongli
dialogues.text: For instance, who is to say that some of Lang-Gan's magnificent jade did not become part of the very foundations upon which Liyue Harbor now stands?

dialogues.speaker: Zhongli
dialogues.text: It is conceivable that this ritual was transmitted in such a manner, too.
Now, now... Let's not let ourselves get carried away. For all its splendor, do not forget that in the end, even Lang-Gan could not escape its heaven-sent fate.
Alas, it is just a pity that the little creatures of this world may never again lift their eyes to the moon, even should misfortune befall them...
But you, Geo Lord, now that you rule this realm — why take the trouble, not to mention the risk, to visit one who bears such profound guilt as I?
Are you not afraid that you might be sullied by the curse of time that was laid upon me?

dialogues.speaker: Zhongli
dialogues.text: There is no risk to speak of — at least, not in comparison to that which you took when you defied the heavens all that time ago.
Tch. As I have stated, time and again, it was not I who defied the heavens.

dialogues.speaker: Zijiao
dialogues.text: Geo Lord, the ancient affairs of Lang-Gan have nothing to do with me, for I am but one of her Deadly Selves, severed before her demise. My name is not Zibai, but Zijiao.

dialogues.speaker: Zijiao
dialogues.text: Surely you did not take us for one and the same solely on the basis that we may all assume the form of white horses?

dialogues.speaker: Zijiao
dialogues.text: Sorry to break it to you, but you seem to have found yourself the wrong white horse.

dialogues.speaker: Zijiao
dialogues.text: Anyway, do tell me — what urgent matter brings you here?

dialogues.speaker: Zhongli
dialogues.text: Very well, then... I have come to ask for Zibai's shade.

dialogues.speaker: Zijiao
dialogues.text: Oh? So the Geo Lord has set his sights upon Zibai's human soul... And what is it that you intend to do with it?

dialogues.speaker: Zhongli
dialogues.text: The world outside is changing. With the new moon's birth, the confines of the shadowmoon are gradually disintegrating. In other words, the Heavenly Soul is set to return.

dialogues.speaker: Zhongli
dialogues.text: Consequently, strange phenomena have manifested within Lang-Gan's former domain, leading to the Earthly Soul's reappearance as well. The last of the trio, the Human Soul, is in your possession.

dialogues.speaker: Zijiao
dialogues.text: Most intriguing...

dialogues.speaker: Zhongli
dialogues.text: My intention is to gather all three together so that an old friend may finally make her return.

dialogues.speaker: Zijiao
dialogues.text: I must admit, it seems that some remarkable affairs are coming to pass in the outside world. Yet there is one thing you seem to have overlooked, Lord of Geo.

dialogues.speaker: Zijiao
dialogues.text: Back in the day, it was you that freed me from that painting — and afterwards, I took up arms in your name. Together, we first subdued Chenyu Vale, then brought peace to Mt. Qingce. It was for this cause that the contract between us was made.

dialogues.speaker: Zijiao
dialogues.text: But now that the debt has been repaid, what cause have you to expect my aid?

dialogues.speaker: Zhongli
dialogues.text: Zibai and I have long been friends. Given not only that you were manifested from a corrupt desire within her divine form, but that you also possess a fragment of her soul, how can you purport to be "the wrong" white horse?

dialogues.speaker: Zijiao
dialogues.text: Ha... I think you'll find that we are now as separate and distinct as any two beings ever were. What once shone with radiant purity has long become dust... what you see is no longer what it was.

dialogues.speaker: Zijiao
dialogues.text: O great Lord of Geo, should this still be unclear to you, I bid you take your leave.

dialogues.speaker: Zhongli
dialogues.text: Mm... It seems that the fault lies in my own lack of consideration. As you wish, I shall let this matter rest.

dialogues.speaker: Zijiao
dialogues.text: Wait... One moment, if you will. Should this not be your opportunity to propose a new contract? The part where you make me an offer I simply couldn't refuse?

dialogues.speaker: Zijiao
dialogues.text: Even those puny mortals know how to haggle when striking their bargains. Should you, the famed God of Contracts, not likewise strive for success through negotiation?

dialogues.speaker: Zijiao
dialogues.text: Come now, enough with the posturing. It's time to name your price.

dialogues.speaker: Zhongli
dialogues.text: Very well. I had, in truth, prepared a new contract for your consideration.

dialogues.speaker: Zijiao
dialogues.text: Hah! I knew you would not come before me unprepared.

dialogues.speaker: Zijiao
dialogues.text: Yet you should know that I want for nothing, for I live in the mountains carefree and untroubled. Occasionally, I even find sport in teasing the mortals who stumble into my presence.

dialogues.speaker: Zhongli
dialogues.text: Then why persist in telling them those ancient stories? I speak of what transpired before the sky collapsed and the earth sank into itself.

dialogues.speaker: Zijiao
dialogues.text: That is merely my way of passing the time. And what of it? Would any believe, much less remember, the ramblings of a mountain hermit?

dialogues.speaker: Zhongli
dialogues.text: Those tales have long since spread throughout the mortal realm.

dialogues.speaker: Zhongli
dialogues.text: Should my words prove insufficient, I invite you to see the world for yourself. To this end, I have found you a pair of trusty guides.

dialogues.speaker: Zhongli
dialogues.text: The Lantern Rite is presently underway in Liyue, and should prove quite intriguing for you.

dialogues.speaker: Zijiao
dialogues.text: So this, then, is the "contract" you have prepared for me?

dialogues.speaker: Zhongli
dialogues.text: Indeed it is. Think of it as... a contract for a one-day festive excursion.

dialogues.speaker: Zijiao
dialogues.text: Surely you do not hope to offer this in exchange for Zibai's shade? The foundation of my very existence for a little excursion seems a little steep, wouldn't you say?

dialogues.speaker: Zhongli
dialogues.text: Why not see for yourself? You can always decide afterwards. The final determination, of course, shall rest with you.

dialogues.speaker: Zijiao
dialogues.text: Is that so? Then perhaps this deal might not be entirely off the table, after all. Hmm... Where, then, are these "guides" of which you speak?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hey, it's Zhongli! We've been looking for you everywhere... We thought you might've gone missing!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: And this is...?

dialogues.speaker: Zhongli
dialogues.text: You're here.

dialogues.speaker: Zijiao
dialogues.text: So these are my guides? Well, well... They certainly look the part, I'll give you that.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: G—Guides...?

dialogues.speaker: Zijiao
dialogues.text: Oh, you poor, innocent little creatures. The benevolent Lord of Geo has sold you to me — which means that for the rest of this day, you belong to me.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Sold us to you!? Just what have you gotten us into, Zhongli?

dialogues.speaker: Zhongli
dialogues.text: The situation is not quite as dire as that would sound. I ask only that you accompany my adeptus friend on a tour of Liyue.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: And you'll help us after that?

dialogues.speaker: Zijiao
dialogues.text: I would suspect that depends on how well you entertain me.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: E—Entertain you!?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Where would you like us to take you?

dialogues.speaker: Zijiao
dialogues.text: Let us start with this "Liyue Harbor" of which I have heard so much. Nowhere is quite so fascinating as a place teeming with little mortals.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: How come this adeptus... sounds so different from what Paimon imagined...?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Let's just play this by ear...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Okay, we'll take care of it! Get ready to find out why they call Paimon the best travel guide in all of Teyvat!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Look, we've arrived at Liyue Harbor!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Not only is it Teyvat's busiest port, it's also the beating heart of Liyue!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: So, dear madam adeptus, where would you like to go first?

dialogues.speaker: Zijiao
dialogues.text: "With humble fare and wine to sip, in comfort clothed and soul at ease, one eats, and all the heart's ills cease."

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hehe, so we're heading straight for the good stuff? Well, you're in luck, 'cause Paimon's an expert when it comes to food!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: There are two main cooking styles in Liyue — Li Cuisine, which is all about mountain delicacies, and Yue Cuisine, which is centered on seafood. The most famous restaurants are Liuli Pavilion and Xinyue Kiosk.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oooh, now Paimon's starting to drool... Guess our only option is to go try them both — two meals, back to back!

dialogues.speaker: Zijiao
dialogues.text: Both sound like excellent options to me. Are these the kind of establishments that most people might visit on a regular basis?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hmm, not exactly... Both Li Cuisine and Yue Cuisine are known for their pricey ingredients. Definitely not what you'd call the budget options!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: But don't you worry about that — just think of it as Zhongli's little treat!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Kinda putting Hu Tao in a tough spot here, Paimon...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: C'mon, aren't you supposed to be pals with Hu Tao? Paimon's sure we can afford to spend a little more of her Mora, at least...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Just looking for an excuse to gorge yourself at someone else's expense, huh?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hey! All Paimon wants is to provide our adeptus with the best possible experience here! Don't you want that too?

dialogues.speaker: Zijiao
dialogues.text: Both certainly sound like worthy choices.

dialogues.speaker: Zijiao
dialogues.text: Just now, though, I happened to see a porter pass this way. Where might individuals like him go to eat?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: A hungry porter, huh? Hmm... Oh, oh, Paimon knows just the place!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Wanmin Restaurant.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Yup! Nothing fancy-schmancy there — just tasty dishes made with simple ingredients in a variety of different styles. Most importantly, it's great value for money too! No wonder everyone loves it, huh?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh, and the owner happens to be a good friend of ours, too!

dialogues.speaker: Zijiao
dialogues.text: "Wanmin Restaurant," hmm... Yes, even the name itself feels lively and down to earth. Alright, let's make it our first stop.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Yippee, that's a great choice too! Alrighty, let's head over there right away — Paimon can't wait to dig in!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wanmin Restaurant, here we come!

talks.objective: Have a meal at Wanmin Restaurant

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Xiangling! Chef Mao! We're here!

dialogues.speaker: Chef Mao
dialogues.text: Oh, hello there! What a surprise to see you two! Welcome, welcome!

dialogues.speaker: Xiangling
dialogues.text: #Hey there, {NICKNAME} and Paimon! We're a little busy today, so grab a table while you still can!

dialogues.speaker: Xiangling
dialogues.text: Um, but... I don't think I've met this lady before? Is she a new friend?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Uh... You could say that...?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: We brought her here for Lantern Rite.

dialogues.speaker: Xiangling
dialogues.text: #Oh, I see... Well, hey there! A friend of {NICKNAME}'s a friend of mine too! Don't worry, we'll take good care of you. Just order whatever you want — it's on the house!

dialogues.speaker: Xiangling
dialogues.text: By the way, I'm Xiangling! I cook here at Wanmin Restaurant. What's your name?

dialogues.speaker: Zijiao
dialogues.text: Miss Xiangling, have you ever heard of the White Horse Adeptus?

dialogues.speaker: Xiangling
dialogues.text: Of course! What about her?

dialogues.speaker: Zijiao
dialogues.text: I am her, and she is me.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh!?

dialogues.speaker: Xiangling
dialogues.text: Y—You mean... you're an Adeptus!?

dialogues.speaker: Chef Mao
dialogues.text: Hahaha, you young-uns crack me up! C'mon Xiangling, you've gotta keep up with the times!

dialogues.speaker: Chef Mao
dialogues.text: Haven't you heard of "cosplay"? It's like a roleplaying game where you dress up as famous characters and pretend to be 'em. Seriously, it's all the rage, and it looks like this young lady's quite the expert!

dialogues.speaker: Chef Mao
dialogues.text: #Your friends sure keep their fingers on the pulse, huh, {NICKNAME}?

dialogues.speaker: Xiangling
dialogues.text: Wow, Dad, didn't know you were so tuned in! But... how come I haven't heard about it?

dialogues.speaker: Chef Mao
dialogues.text: You gotta listen to our customers! Didn't I tell you to spend less time chasing after wild vegetables and more time making friends? You're even more out of touch than I am, haha...

dialogues.speaker: Xiangling
dialogues.text: Hey, I like making friends too! Isn't that what I'm doing right now?

dialogues.speaker: Xiangling
dialogues.text: Anyway... Even if it is just a costume, is it alright if I still call you "White Horse Adeptus"?

dialogues.speaker: Zijiao
dialogues.text: Of course it's "alright," because that's exactly who I am.

dialogues.speaker: Xiangling
dialogues.text: Hehe, okay, okay... I can see you're really committed to the role! How about I call you "The Real White Horse Adeptus" instead?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #Hah... In that case, you can call Paimon "The Real {NICKNAME}"!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Guess that makes me "The Real Paimon."

dialogues.speaker: Xiangling
dialogues.text: Haha, yeah right. You could've at least switched outfits!

dialogues.speaker: Zijiao
dialogues.text: Hmph, puny mortals. Nevertheless, I suppose it might be amusing to indulge in your little charade, for a while at least...

dialogues.speaker: Xiangling
dialogues.text: Alright, go grab yourselves a table! I'll come take your order in a bit.

talks.objective: Take a seat behind the restaurant

dialogues.speaker: Lu Xiangxiang
dialogues.text: Hello... May I ask if Miss Xiangling and Chef Mao are here?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Yeah, they're just over there! Wait a sec, aren't you...?

dialogues.speaker: Xiangling
dialogues.text: So, what would you like to— Huh? You're...

dialogues.speaker: Lu Xiangxiang
dialogues.text: Hello, Miss Xiangling... It's me, Lu Xiangxiang. The one who broke some stuff here at your restaurant a few days ago.

dialogues.speaker: Lu Xiangxiang
dialogues.text: I just wanted you to know how sorry I am... I honestly don't know what came over me. Please, please forgive me...

dialogues.speaker: Chef Mao
dialogues.text: Oh, it's you! You really gave me a fright that day, young lady! You didn't actually get food poisoning from our Black-Back Perch Stew, right...?

dialogues.speaker: Xiangling
dialogues.text: C'mon Dad, she's come to say sorry...

dialogues.speaker: Xiangling
dialogues.text: It's alright, Miss Lu. You must've been feeling a bit off that day. You're looking so much better now, though!

dialogues.speaker: Xiangling
dialogues.text: Why don't you grab a table too? This one's on the house!

dialogues.speaker: Lu Xiangxiang
dialogues.text: No, I couldn't possibly...

dialogues.speaker: Xiangling
dialogues.text: Hey, it's totally okay! We all feel under the weather sometimes, especially when we're away from home. Go on, find yourself a—

dialogues.speaker: Xiangling
dialogues.text: ...Uh, yikes, looks like all the tables are taken...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wanna come sit with us? We've got an extra seat over here!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Must be fate, huh?

dialogues.speaker: Xiangling
dialogues.text: Thanks guys! So, what would you like to eat today? Feel free to order anything you like!

dialogues.speaker: Zijiao
dialogues.text: Hmm... I should very much like to sample your renowned Poisonous Black-Back Perch Stew.

dialogues.speaker: Lu Xiangxiang
dialogues.text: I—It wasn't poisoned... That was all on me...

dialogues.speaker: Xiangling
dialogues.text: Ahaha... So that's one portion of Black-Back Perch Stew. How about you guys?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Paimon wants... Uh...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Since it's on the house, why don't you choose for us?

dialogues.speaker: Xiangling
dialogues.text: Sure thing! Looks like Paimon's having trouble making up her mind, hehe... Anyway, I guarantee you'll love it!

dialogues.speaker: Xiangling
dialogues.text: Let me think... Well, since the Black-Back Perch Stew is on the spicier side, I guess it makes sense to balance it out with a serving of Stir-Fried Shrimp.

dialogues.speaker: Xiangling
dialogues.text: And since it's Lantern Rite season, you'd better try out the Triple-Layered Consommé and Come and Get It too. Those are our seasonal specialties!

dialogues.speaker: Xiangling
dialogues.text: As for the carbs... since we've got a full table, how about some Right at Home along with our special Chili-Mince Cornbread Buns? Trust me, you won't be disappointed!

dialogues.speaker: Xiangling
dialogues.text: Then, for dessert, I'll whip you up some Lucky Snow Delight. I just came up with it a few days ago... and I can't wait for you to try it!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wow, sounds like quite the feast! Looks like Paimon's in luck today!

dialogues.speaker: Lu Xiangxiang
dialogues.text: Am I the only one who thinks that's... way too much?

dialogues.speaker: Xiangling
dialogues.text: Not at all! Don't worry, I know what I'm doing. And to top it all off, our star dish, Adeptus' Temptation! Hehe, you should know that we don't often serve this here at Wanmin Restaurant...

dialogues.speaker: Xiangling
dialogues.text: But since this is my first time cooking for the "White Horse Adeptus," I'm pulling out all the stops!

dialogues.speaker: Xiangling
dialogues.text: Okie-dokie, just sit back and relax. I'll have your dishes out in no time!

dialogues.speaker: Lu Xiangxiang
dialogues.text: Hold on... Did I just hear Miss Xiangling mention the White Horse Adeptus?

dialogues.speaker: Zijiao
dialogues.text: You did indeed, and you're looking right at her.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Ahem... That's a joke by the way... She's cosplaying!

dialogues.speaker: Lu Xiangxiang
dialogues.text: Oh, I see... Phew, almost believed you there for a moment!

dialogues.speaker: Zijiao
dialogues.text: Tell me, little one — what business might you have with the White Horse Adeptus?

dialogues.speaker: Lu Xiangxiang
dialogues.text: Mm... It's a long story. Basically, a while back, I took part in an archaeological dig over at The Chasm. While we were there, we discovered a number of relics.

dialogues.speaker: Lu Xiangxiang
dialogues.text: Our findings show that they date back to the era of Lang-Gan, an ancient nation whose people are said to have been the ancestors of some of the modern-day inhabitants of Chenyu Vale.

dialogues.speaker: Zijiao
dialogues.text: And why might such matters concern the White Horse Adeptus?

dialogues.speaker: Lu Xiangxiang
dialogues.text: Because some of those relics not only seem to contain textual references to her, but even depictions of what she looked like.

dialogues.speaker: Lu Xiangxiang
dialogues.text: There have long been legends claiming that the White Horse Adeptus was a deity of that era, but there are plenty of other theories out there too.

dialogues.speaker: Lu Xiangxiang
dialogues.text: If I could just locate some more detailed records, I'm sure we'd be able to find out so much more...

dialogues.speaker: Zijiao
dialogues.text: So, you're into history?

dialogues.speaker: Lu Xiangxiang
dialogues.text: I... Well, to tell you the truth, I actually joined the archaeological team by sheer accident. But once I'd started down this path, I knew that I wanted to make something of myself.

dialogues.speaker: Lu Xiangxiang
dialogues.text: Recently, though, things seem to have taken a turn for the worse... *sigh* Still can't believe I caused such a mess, and even ended up hurting someone...

dialogues.speaker: Zijiao
dialogues.text: Oh? So you're considering becoming a martial artist now instead?

dialogues.speaker: Lu Xiangxiang
dialogues.text: No, no, I mean, they weren't seriously hurt! It was just a few scratches, and they let it go after my mother compensated them...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: You know, that really wasn't your fault...

dialogues.speaker: Lu Xiangxiang
dialogues.text: *sigh* Either way, my career's pretty much over. And even though both the victim and the Ministry of Civil Affairs say they won't be pursuing the matter any further, my father says he's going to punish me according to our family rules.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: F—Family rules!?

dialogues.speaker: Lu Xiangxiang
dialogues.text: Yeah, he's decided to ground me. I'll have to return to Qiaoying Village after Lantern Rite, and goodness knows when I'll be allowed to leave again...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wow, that's harsh! Sounds like the kind of thing only rich, super traditional parents would do...

dialogues.speaker: Lu Xiangxiang
dialogues.text: We're not exactly "rich," though! All we own are a few tea fields in Qiaoying Village and a guesthouse in Liyue Harbor...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: A guesthouse? It isn't... Baiju Guesthouse, by any chance?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Ahh, so Boss Lu must be your...

dialogues.speaker: Lu Xiangxiang
dialogues.text: Yep, he's my grandfather! So you've heard of the guesthouse before?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Small world, huh?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Come to think of it, didn't Boss Lu mention something about... hoping that the White Horse Adeptus would show up and "let her divine power be known"?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (Well, she showed up alright...)

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Sure, but... Paimon's guessing this wasn't exactly what he had in mind...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (Shh, keep it down...)

dialogues.speaker: Zijiao
dialogues.text: Little one, it sounds to me that your family is rather well-off, after all. What, then, drew you to archaeology? Why subject yourself to such unnecessary hardships?

dialogues.speaker: Lu Xiangxiang
dialogues.text: Even if I stayed at home, there's no guarantee I'd lead a nice, easy life. Just look at my father.

dialogues.speaker: Lu Xiangxiang
dialogues.text: Recently, my grandfather put him in charge of the guesthouse, and he came up with a bunch of ideas right away, starting with changing its name.

dialogues.speaker: Lu Xiangxiang
dialogues.text: That didn't turn out well, though. My grandfather yelled at him for days, even calling him a bad son, and they still haven't let it go...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Ohhh... Paimon thinks we might've heard about that, too...

dialogues.speaker: Lu Xiangxiang
dialogues.text: Long story short... Being dependent on others is never fun. You just end up being completely under their thumb.

dialogues.speaker: Lu Xiangxiang
dialogues.text: That's why I want to make it on my own out here, no matter how hard it is. After all, as the saying goes, "to rise above others, one must endure the hardest of hardships."

dialogues.speaker: Zijiao
dialogues.text: Hahaha...

dialogues.speaker: Lu Xiangxiang
dialogues.text: What's... so funny about that?

dialogues.speaker: Zijiao
dialogues.text: You poor, innocent little creatures never fail to amuse me. To think you would endure all manner of hardships in your brief time on this mortal plane, and all that merely to "rise above others"!

dialogues.speaker: Zijiao
dialogues.text: I would have thought that the wiser path would be to simply roam this world as I do.

dialogues.speaker: Lu Xiangxiang
dialogues.text: Huh?

dialogues.speaker: Zijiao
dialogues.text: Tell me, what is it that you truly delight in? Archaeology? Martial arts? Tea-planting? Or perhaps the keeping of a guesthouse?

dialogues.speaker: Lu Xiangxiang
dialogues.text: What I... delight in?

dialogues.speaker: Zijiao
dialogues.text: Yes. Surely there must be something you don't find quite so exhausting? Whatever delights you should not feel like a burden.

dialogues.speaker: Lu Xiangxiang
dialogues.text: But... do things like that really exist?

dialogues.speaker: Zijiao
dialogues.text: Of course! Take Miss Xiangling, for instance — I defy you to detect even a hint of hardship on her face when she wields her wok and spatula.

dialogues.speaker: Zijiao
dialogues.text: So, since it seems you are resolved to tread the rocky path, you should strive with all your might to pursue that which brings you delight.

dialogues.speaker: Lu Xiangxiang
dialogues.text: You mean... like cosplay?

dialogues.speaker: Zijiao
dialogues.text: *cough* I suppose... you might say that...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh... Looks like the White Horse Adeptus is really getting into her "role"...

dialogues.speaker: Lu Xiangxiang
dialogues.text: Hmm... I think I get what you mean, then. Maybe I should have a chat with Miss Xiangling before I head home...

dialogues.speaker: Xiangling
dialogues.text: Okay everyone, sorry to keep you waiting! Here's your food!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wow! It all smells so good!

dialogues.speaker: Zijiao
dialogues.text: Finally, I get to try that famous poisonous stew...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hey, didn't you hear what Xiangxiang said? It wasn't the stew! If anyone's to blame, it's that other you!

dialogues.speaker: Zijiao
dialogues.text: Whew...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: What's... up?

dialogues.speaker: Zijiao
dialogues.text: How fiercely this mortal fare burns upon the tongue!

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: You and the others devour the food set before you...

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: Once you've all finished, Lu Xiangxiang stays behind to ask Xiangling how she might discover a vocation she truly loves.

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: The rest of you make your way onto the streets as you discuss the next stop on your one-day tour of Liyue.

talks.objective: Think about where to go next

dialogues.speaker: Zijiao
dialogues.text: Mmm... Most satisfying, as poisonous stews go. So, where to now? Time, I think, to seek out some diversion.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh, there's plenty of entertainment options in Liyue, Paimon'll tell ya that! The locals like to drink tea, walk their pets, play chess, watch operas, attend storytelling performances—

dialogues.speaker: Zijiao
dialogues.text: Storytelling performances...?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Y'know, like... listening to people telling stories! They're usually based on old Liyue legends, just like their operas.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Stuff like "The Divine Damsel of Devastation," "Through the Eyes of a Dragon," or "The Sanctification of Tao Dou"...

dialogues.speaker: Zijiao
dialogues.text: What about the story of the bright moon that sits in the sky above us?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hmm, Paimon doesn't think she's heard that one... Still, the moon does come up quite a lot! It's even in the name itself — the "yue" in "Liyue" actually means "moon"!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Since we're on the subject... You like telling stories yourself, right? Why don't we go check it out?

dialogues.speaker: Zijiao
dialogues.text: In that case, I'll have to trouble the two of you to lead the way.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Awesome, let's go! Third-Round Knockout, here we come!

dialogues.speaker: Iron Tongue Tian
dialogues.text: What a tongue twister... Phew, I'd have made a complete fool of myself if I'd tried to say it on stage without practicing it first.

dialogues.speaker: Iron Tongue Tian
dialogues.text: "Ha! Call yourself 'Iron Tongue Tian'? 'Wobbly Tongue Tian,' more like!"

dialogues.speaker: Yun Jin
dialogues.text: Heh, I used to have that problem a lot...

dialogues.speaker: Yun Jin
dialogues.text: But if you just take your time to grasp the meaning and commit it to memory, you'll be able to say it smoothly in no time.

dialogues.speaker: Iron Tongue Tian
dialogues.text: You're right, Ms. Yun. I'll give it another try...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hey, Yun Jin! Fancy seeing you here! What are you two talking about?

dialogues.speaker: Yun Jin
dialogues.text: #Ah, {NICKNAME} and Paimon, we meet again. And who, may I ask, is this...?

dialogues.speaker: Zijiao
dialogues.text: You may call me the White Horse Adeptus.

dialogues.speaker: Iron Tongue Tian
dialogues.text: The White Horse Adeptus!?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: *cough* She's not... really an adeptus...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: ...She's just cosplaying as one.

dialogues.speaker: Yun Jin
dialogues.text: I see... Well, it certainly looks like a lot of fun!

dialogues.speaker: Iron Tongue Tian
dialogues.text: Oh! Funny you mention it, this type of thing is actually something I'm quite familiar with.

dialogues.speaker: Iron Tongue Tian
dialogues.text: Once, to perform "Through the Eyes of a Dragon," I decided to imagine that I was Rex Lapis himself, hahaha. It was the only way to truly inhabit his mindset and understand his resolve to quell those demons...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Sounds like you just wanted an excuse to feel all big and powerful...

dialogues.speaker: Iron Tongue Tian
dialogues.text: Hey, that's... You just don't understand how inspiration works!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #Hmph, you're one to talk! Paimon's traveled all over with {NICKNAME}, and she's seen things that would make your jaw drop!

dialogues.speaker: Iron Tongue Tian
dialogues.text: Alright then, since you claim to be so knowledgeable, why don't you prove it by reciting "An Ancient Poem"?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: An ancient poem? Which one?

dialogues.speaker: Iron Tongue Tian
dialogues.text: Hah, see! You mean to tell me you've never even heard of the ancient poem called "An Ancient Poem"?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: What kind of a title is that!?

dialogues.speaker: Yun Jin
dialogues.text: Ha, quit teasing Paimon. We only just found out about that ourselves. He's talking about the writing on those ancient relics.

dialogues.speaker: Yun Jin
dialogues.text: When we first saw it, we couldn't figure out what it all meant, so in the meantime, we decided to just refer to it as "An Ancient Poem."

dialogues.speaker: Yun Jin
dialogues.text: However, thanks to the painstaking work of the scholars who were tasked with decoding it, it seems like that's exactly what it was — or rather, an ode offered in veneration of the moon and the White Horse Adeptus.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Ohhh yeah, didn't Keqing mention that before? It's got something to do with Lang-Gan, right?

dialogues.speaker: Yun Jin
dialogues.text: That is correct. The Ministry of Civil Affairs has issued a notice stating that, although it is true that the moon may disappear tonight, we should be in no danger. In other words, there's nothing to fear.

dialogues.speaker: Yun Jin
dialogues.text: But if you're worried, we can always take a leaf from the book of the ancients — by reciting this poem, I mean, and calling for the White Horse Adeptus' aid. If we do that, I'm certain she'll protect our moon and keep us safe.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Whoa, seriously? Paimon has to get a look at this...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: "Under moon eternal, in radiant night, a maiden grants silk... soft and light?" What in Teyvat's that supposed to mean...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: "Under moon iridescent, in night divine... Blablabla something cloth so fine."

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: "Something about fields being plowed, something else about seeds being sown... from the earth..." Seriously, what is this?

dialogues.speaker: Zijiao
dialogues.text: "The fields are plowed, the seeds are sown, and from the earth, life is grown."

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: ...Whoa, you did that without even looking!

dialogues.speaker: Iron Tongue Tian
dialogues.text: Bravo, bravo! We have an expert in our midst!

dialogues.speaker: Iron Tongue Tian
dialogues.text: Looks like this young lady really does know her role inside out, haha! If I didn't know any better, I'd have taken her for the real deal!

dialogues.speaker: Zijiao
dialogues.text: That's because I am "the real deal."

dialogues.speaker: Iron Tongue Tian
dialogues.text: That's the spirit! This is exactly the kind of mindset I was talking about! "Behold, mortals, I am none other than the indomitable Rex Lapis himself! Kneel before my godly splendor!"

dialogues.speaker: Iron Tongue Tian
dialogues.text: Believe me, young lady, I know exactly why you do it. Back in the day, I was just like you...

dialogues.speaker: Zijiao
dialogues.text: I must say, you are rather amusing, as mortals go.

dialogues.speaker: Yun Jin
dialogues.text: Miss "White Horse Adeptus," it is a great pleasure to make your acquaintance today. I have some questions regarding the poem, and I was wondering, perhaps, if you might be able to shed some light on it?

dialogues.speaker: Zijiao
dialogues.text: Hmm, you want me to... explain the full meaning of its verses?

dialogues.speaker: Yun Jin
dialogues.text: Your guidance would be much appreciated.

dialogues.speaker: Zijiao
dialogues.text: Fascinating... Tell me, do all the people of Liyue still express such reverence for the ancient ways?

dialogues.speaker: Yun Jin
dialogues.text: Well, it's true that we hold a deep fondness for our history — but it is hardly our only pursuit. One of my good friends, for instance, is even more devoted to the modern Fontainian art of rock 'n' roll.

dialogues.speaker: Iron Tongue Tian
dialogues.text: Exactly! And don't forget, great practitioners of the roleplaying arts walk among us too — people like me and you, young lady!

dialogues.speaker: Yun Jin
dialogues.text: Haha, yes... So rather than placing too much emphasis on our reverence for the ancient ways, it might be better to say that here in Liyue, a hundred passions bloom, each with a voice of its own.

dialogues.speaker: Zijiao
dialogues.text: I see... Then I suppose it wouldn't do any harm for me to enlighten you. In truth, it is but a simple poem of blessings. Its meaning is this:

dialogues.speaker: Zijiao
dialogues.text: "As the Eternal Moon rises in the night sky, a maiden adorned with lustrous jade descends upon the earth. She blesses the kudzu vines and mulberry leaves, so that they may be used to make coarse cloth that is nevertheless soft, light, and comfortable to wear."

dialogues.speaker: Zijiao
dialogues.text: "As the Iridescent Moon rises in the night sky, a maiden adorned with lustrous jade descends upon the earth. She blesses the kudzu vines and hemp, so that they may be used to make fine, luxurious cloth."

dialogues.speaker: Zijiao
dialogues.text: "As the Frost Moon rises in the night sky, a maiden adorned with lustrous jade descends upon the earth. She blesses the mugwort and artemisia, so that they may be perfect for divination."

dialogues.speaker: Yun Jin
dialogues.text: So she really did come down from the moon...?

dialogues.speaker: Zijiao
dialogues.text: "She shows the people how to use the plow and spade to purge the land of weeds, till the soil, and heap up the earth to make it fertile; then with the hoe, she teaches them to sow their grain, bestowing the promise of life upon every seed."

dialogues.speaker: Zijiao
dialogues.text: "She blesses the millet and the beans, ensuring that their stalks and vines stretch forth without end. She graces the wheat and the rice, so that their heavy heads are filled with plump, glistening grain."

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Sounds like she's a real pro at all this farming stuff!

dialogues.speaker: Zijiao
dialogues.text: "The fruits of the field are harvested and brewed into sacred wine for honored guests. This we reverently present to the divine maiden, with every ceremonial step flawlessly observed, so that she may witness the depth of our piety and respect."

dialogues.speaker: Zijiao
dialogues.text: "O, divine maiden, how can your graceful presence in the sky not seem like that of a fairy descending from the heavens?"

dialogues.speaker: Zijiao
dialogues.text: "O, divine maiden, how does your pure and radiant form not resemble the guardian spirit of our land?"

dialogues.speaker: Zijiao
dialogues.text: "I send my heart's desire ascending to the heavens, beseeching you to grant us good fortune and blessings in the coming year."

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh, so that's what it's supposed to mean...?

dialogues.speaker: Iron Tongue Tian
dialogues.text: I find myself speechless... moved beyond the power of words to convey. Oh young lady, haha, you have shown me the heights to which a true role-player might aspire!

dialogues.speaker: Yun Jin
dialogues.text: A truly remarkable performance! I did not anticipate that anyone could unravel this poem with such depth and clarity, and so soon after the Ministry of Civil Affairs' notice too.

dialogues.speaker: Yun Jin
dialogues.text: I'd even begun to consider myself somewhat versed in the matter, but as they say, there's always someone more knowledgeable out there. Allow me to extend my thanks to you, Miss "White Horse Adeptus."

dialogues.speaker: Zijiao
dialogues.text: You are far too humble, young one. I must confess, it is I who have been surprised — not only by you, but also by this "Liyue Harbor" of the present day...

dialogues.speaker: Yun Jin
dialogues.text: Ah, so you're not from Liyue? And what, may I ask, has surprised you about it?

dialogues.speaker: Zijiao
dialogues.text: Oh, it's nothing, really. Just some old memories scattered here and there.

dialogues.speaker: Zijiao
dialogues.text: Very well, my guides. I suppose it is time we set forth on the next part of our excursion. I'd like to go see that wharf now. What say the two of you?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: N—No problem! We'll take you wherever you want!

dialogues.speaker: Yun Jin
dialogues.text: Oh, leaving so soon? Before you go, allow me to introduce myself... I am Yun Jin, director of the Yun-Han Opera Troupe. May I ask your name in return?

dialogues.speaker: Zijiao
dialogues.text: Heh, my own "name" is scarcely worth mentioning. But since you asked, hmm... perhaps I'll tell you the title of that poem instead.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh? So it isn't actually called "An Ancient Poem"?

dialogues.speaker: Zijiao
dialogues.text: Ha, of course not! Its real title is "Odes of Lang: Zibai."

dialogues.speaker: Yun Jin
dialogues.text: "Odes of Lang"... "Zibai"...

dialogues.speaker: Zijiao
dialogues.text: Mhm... Alright then. Until we meet again.

talks.objective: Go to where the Mingxiao Lantern is

dialogues.speaker: Yanfei
dialogues.text: Hey, Ganyu! I almost forgot to mention — on my recent trip to Nod-Krai, I came across something really fascinating in the Frostmoon Scions' library.

dialogues.speaker: Yanfei
dialogues.text: I found records in their collection of another divine envoy living on the moon!

dialogues.speaker: Ganyu
dialogues.text: A divine envoy on the moon? You don't think it could have been referring to the White Horse Adeptus too, do you?

dialogues.speaker: Yanfei
dialogues.text: No way to say for sure. Still, the similarities between our legends are intriguing, to say the least.

dialogues.speaker: Yanfei
dialogues.text: Isn't it amazing? Especially when you consider how far apart we are...

dialogues.speaker: Ganyu
dialogues.text: It truly is. We might live in different lands, but when we look up at the night sky, we all see the same moon and stars.

dialogues.speaker: Yanfei
dialogues.text: Right? It's like we're all bound together, no matter where we are. When you think of it like that, it's almost as if our friends from other nations will be right here, celebrating with us! Isn't that a wonderful thought?

dialogues.speaker: Ganyu
dialogues.text: No wonder you were so excited to go see the giant lantern when you first got back. Sounds like you're a real fan of the White Horse Adeptus, huh?

dialogues.speaker: Yanfei
dialogues.text: I guess you could say that, haha! Just a pity she's so elusive... Even Granny's never met her, y'know. Maybe she really is just a legend, after all.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hey, Yanfei and Ganyu! Trust Paimon — the White Horse Adeptus is as real as real can be!

dialogues.speaker: Yanfei
dialogues.text: #Huh? Oh look, it's {NICKNAME} and Paimon! Feels like I haven't seen you two in, like... forever. Happy Lantern Rite! It's so good to see you again.

dialogues.speaker: Ganyu
dialogues.text: Hey, you two! Happy Lantern Rite!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Happy Lantern Rite!

dialogues.speaker: Yanfei
dialogues.text: Did I... hear you right just now, Paimon? Does that mean you've actually seen the White Horse Adeptus!?

dialogues.speaker: Zijiao
dialogues.text: She has indeed. And now, so have you.

dialogues.speaker: Ganyu
dialogues.text: Huh? And you are...?

dialogues.speaker: Zijiao
dialogues.text: Why, who else? The White Horse Adeptus, of course.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Could you maybe... start with something else next time?

dialogues.speaker: Yanfei
dialogues.text: *gasp* Y—You're the White Horse Adeptus!?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: *cough* She's cosplaying as the White Horse Adeptus.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: ...That's right! Allow Paimon to introduce you to our new friend, Zijiao! She's been lowkey obsessed with cosplaying the White Horse Adeptus, ever since we met her...

dialogues.speaker: Yanfei
dialogues.text: Haha, I see! Well then... Greetings, Miss Zijiao. My name is Yanfei, and recently, I've been "lowkey obsessed" with learning everything I can about the White Horse Adeptus.

dialogues.speaker: Ganyu
dialogues.text: I'm sure the two of you will get along like a house on fire... Oh, and by the way, I'm Ganyu.

dialogues.speaker: Yanfei
dialogues.text: So, Miss Zijiao! You must be here to see the giant lantern too, right?

dialogues.speaker: Zijiao
dialogues.text: Hmm? A horse-shaped Xiao Lantern... Is that... what I think it is?

dialogues.speaker: Yanfei
dialogues.text: That's right! A lantern made to honor the White Horse Adeptus herself! Isn't it gorgeous?

dialogues.speaker: Zijiao
dialogues.text: *chuckle*

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh? What are you laughing at?

dialogues.speaker: Zijiao
dialogues.text: Both the lantern... and myself.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: What do you mean?

dialogues.speaker: Zijiao
dialogues.text: This lantern truly is an artistic masterpiece, but tell me this — have any of you ever seen a horse before?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #Uh... Come to think of it, Paimon can't remember ever actually seeing one herself. What about you, {NICKNAME}?

response.speaker: Zijiao
response.text: This horse appears to be mid-trot, but it has adopted what is called a "lateral gait" — where the legs on one side of the body move together in unison. A rather rare sight, indeed...

response.speaker: Zijiao
response.text: Just now, I suddenly pictured myself... I mean, the White Horse Adeptus running the same way. The image was so absurd, I could barely contain my mirth...

response.speaker: Yanfei
response.text: Oh, really? I never knew that... You learn something every day, huh!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: ...Oh c'mon, it's basically a giant piece of fan art! Who cares if it's different than the original!

response.speaker: Player
response.text: So... Why laugh at yourself?

response.speaker: Zijiao
response.text: Heh... I was merely laughing at my own ignorance. I came here thinking that the White Horse Adeptus' tale had been long forgotten — yet here I am, gazing upon a lantern made in her honor.

response.speaker: Yanfei
response.text: Hehe, well, you couldn't have been more mistaken! There are so many tales about the White Horse Adeptus, I'm starting to lose count. Just off the top of my head—

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Just so you know, Yanfei, we've heard it all like... a million times before!

response.speaker: Yanfei
response.text: ...Aha, but there's one thing I can guarantee that you haven't!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Huh? You mean like, a new chapter of her story's come to light?

response.speaker: Yanfei
response.text: Mm-hmm, and I heard it from Ganyu just yesterday! Hey, why don't you share it with the others?

response.speaker: Ganyu
response.text: Sure, no problem. Hmm, where to begin... Do you guys still remember what Liyue's Moonchase Festival is about?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Of course! It's a festival held in honor of Guo— Uhh, the Stove God!

response.speaker: Ganyu
response.text: That's right. But it took a really long time for the Stove God Festival to become what it is today.

response.speaker: Ganyu
response.text: In its earliest form, it was actually an adeptal ritual known as the "Moonchase Rite."

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hmm... Paimon remembers Madame Ping mentioning that before, but she never explained exactly what it was.

response.speaker: Ganyu
response.text: According to Cloud Retainer, the Moonchase Rite was originally a ritual meant for communicating with the moon.

response.speaker: Zijiao
response.text: Communicating with the moon...? But for what purpose?

response.speaker: Ganyu
response.text: At first, Cloud Retainer wasn't entirely sure either, as it was always Rex Lapis who performed the ritual.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Whoa, Zhong— Uhh, Rex Lapis did it himself!? Must've been a really important ritual...

response.speaker: Ganyu
response.text: That's right. Unfortunately, despite numerous attempts, they never actually received any response from the moon... which is why they eventually stopped performing it.

response.speaker: Ganyu
response.text: But then, just yesterday, Keqing took a picture of the moon being obscured by a dark hole to Cloud Retainer, and asked if it had anything to do with the Moonchase Rite...

response.speaker: Ganyu
response.text: The moment Cloud Retainer saw it, it suddenly dawned on her that the Rite might have been an attempt to reach the White Horse Adeptus all along...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Does that mean... Zhongli's been trying to bring back the White Horse Adeptus all this time?

response.speaker: Yanfei
response.text: So, how about that? Bet you never thought there might even be a link between the White Horse Adeptus and the Moonchase Festival...

choices.text: It is quite the revelation, yes.

response.speaker: Ganyu
response.text: If Keqing hadn't taken that picture to Cloud Retainer, we would never have known any of this...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: This is probably what Keqing was referring to that day when she mentioned there were some ideas she wanted to follow up on...

response.speaker: Zijiao
response.text: So, Geo Archon... All this time, you've been striving to awaken her...

response.speaker: Yanfei
response.text: Huh? What do you mean, "awaken"?

response.speaker: Zijiao
response.text: ...Nothing. What I truly meant to say was, this new insight you've provided has been truly... eye-opening.

response.speaker: Zijiao
response.text: Oh, by the way, my trusty guides, I've been meaning to ask — where in Liyue Harbor might one enjoy an expansive scenic view?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Huh? We're off to the next stop already? But Paimon's barely done digesting that lore bomb just now!

response.speaker: Zijiao
response.text: All the more reason to find the right spot to let it sink in.

response.speaker: Ganyu
response.text: Oh, so that's what you're up to, a tour of Liyue Harbor? In that case, if you're looking for a spot with a panoramic view, I'd recommend Yujing Terrace.

response.speaker: Yanfei
response.text: That's a great idea! Since the terrace is on higher ground, the sea view from up there's sooo much better.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: I agree.

response.speaker: Yanfei
response.text: Great! Well, the Lantern Rite's about to start, so we should get back to Granny's now.

response.speaker: Ganyu
response.text: Hope to see you all at the festival tonight!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oh, you're off too? Alright then... See you both soon!

response.speaker: Yanfei
response.text: See you soon!

response.speaker: Zijiao
response.text: Very well, my guides — what are we waiting for?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: O—Okay, you're the boss! Yujing Terrace it is — after all, the customer's always right!

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Hold on a second.

response.speaker: Zijiao
response.text: Something else you needed to do?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Let's take a photo here in front of the giant lantern.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Woohoo! Paimon likes that idea!

response.speaker: Zijiao
response.text: And what, may I ask, is a "photo"?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: It's this awesome invention that lets you record moments in the blink of an eye! Except, you've gotta try not to actually blink...

response.speaker: Zijiao
response.text: Oh? What must I do in preparation, then?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #Nothing! All you gotta do is choose a pose — {NICKNAME} will handle everything else.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Come on, let's give it a try!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Look, we got a great picture! Paimon's gonna call it... "The White Horse Adeptus Meets the White Horse Adeptus in Liyue Harbor"!

response.speaker: Zijiao
response.text: Hah, they've even discovered a way to preserve moments in time... Now I truly am curious to witness what else these mortals might accomplish.

response.speaker: Zijiao
response.text: Very well, let us proceed. Yujing Terrace lies in that direction, does it not?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hey, wait for us!

choices.text: Not exactly. It's an idea I've considered before.

dialogues.speaker: Zijiao
dialogues.text: Truly, a marvelous view if ever there was one... It seems the charm of this "Liyue Harbor" is only heightened by the sun's dying light.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Mm-hmm! And soon, people will start releasing their Xiao Lanterns to mark the most important day of the year.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Practically everyone will be with their friends and family, eating a big meal, chatting, and even setting off fireworks. Trust Paimon, it'll look even more amazing then! Whaddaya say, wanna stay to see that?

dialogues.speaker: Zijiao
dialogues.text: Ha, no need. Let us bring this weary day to a close.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: "Weary day"...? You mean... you didn't enjoy your tour?

dialogues.speaker: Zijiao
dialogues.text: I had imagined you would arrange for me to witness some grand spectacle — perhaps the descent of divine beings, the manifestation of the sacred before mortal eyes, or the appearance of a selfless hero come to aid the helpless and downtrodden.

dialogues.speaker: Zijiao
dialogues.text: Or, should that not come to pass, then at the very least, spend a little more coin. For that, it seems, is how one finds true enjoyment.

dialogues.speaker: Zijiao
dialogues.text: Alas, but there was none of these. Instead, we merely filled our bellies, listened to tales, and gazed upon a crude imitation of my likeness. And now, the sun begins its descent.

dialogues.speaker: Zijiao
dialogues.text: What a day of quiet tedium.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: W—We're... so sorry! If we'd known that was what you wanted, we'd have done it all differently!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: It's all that Zhongli's fault for not making the customer's requirements clear!

dialogues.speaker: Zijiao
dialogues.text: Well, it's too late now. Do you still believe I would part with that soul fragment, now so intertwined with my very being?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: B—But...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Quit scaring Paimon already.

dialogues.speaker: Zijiao
dialogues.text: Hm! I knew you were the more astute of the pair.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Eh!? You were just trying to scare Paimon?

dialogues.speaker: Zijiao
dialogues.text: It seems the realm of the Geo Archon has a way of making one more... "stony-faced."

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: So... Y—You were just pulling Paimon's leg?

dialogues.speaker: Zijiao
dialogues.text: Of course. I was merely engaging in a little banter with the two of you.

dialogues.speaker: Zijiao
dialogues.text: Long ago, I shared tales with various mortals who chanced upon my mountain abode. Never did I imagine that those stories would endure... It seems I greatly underestimated them.

dialogues.speaker: Zijiao
dialogues.text: Perhaps, as your Geo Lord said, a few pieces of ancient Lang-Gan's magnificent jade have truly become part of the very foundation of this land.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: So... You've decided to help us?

dialogues.speaker: Zijiao
dialogues.text: Again, that goes without saying. I made up my mind some time ago now.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: And when was that, exactly?

dialogues.speaker: Zijiao
dialogues.text: When I beheld a rather intriguing scene as I set foot in this city.

dialogues.speaker: Zijiao
dialogues.text: I saw porters passing through the alleys, setting down heavy wooden crates from their weary shoulders; peddlers pushing carts, as the kites and lanterns upon them rustled gently in the breeze...

dialogues.speaker: Zijiao
dialogues.text: I saw cooks cooking, actors acting, scholars reading, soldiers marching, children playing, elders resting, officials officiating, and the common folk absorbed in this or that, reveling in the simple joys of life.

dialogues.speaker: Zijiao
dialogues.text: Some, it seems, have already found that which stirs their hearts; while others continue to fret, troubled by uncertain futures.

dialogues.speaker: Zijiao
dialogues.text: Yet in this gentle and serene order, each holds fast to their anticipation — not only for the celebrations to come, but also, for the first light of the morrow.

dialogues.speaker: Zijiao
dialogues.text: Scenes I once yearned to behold now unfold before me — no longer in Lang-Gan, but in Liyue Harbor, thousands of years on.

dialogues.speaker: Zijiao
dialogues.text: Ah... How wondrous is this mortal realm.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Thank you.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Thank you, White Horse Adeptus... Thank you so much!

dialogues.speaker: Zijiao
dialogues.text: Adeptus, adepti... Perhaps the singular art in which we are truly proficient is that of sequestering ourselves within the high mountains.

dialogues.speaker: Zijiao
dialogues.text: But once we leave our mountain refuge, we find ourselves drawn back to mortal ways all the same.

dialogues.speaker: Zijiao
dialogues.text: #So, it is I who should offer my thanks to the two of you. {NICKNAME}, Paimon, you have made this day more delightful than any I've known in a long, long time.

dialogues.speaker: Zijiao
dialogues.text: Come now and take what it is you need.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: You mean... like, right now? B—But... Don't you think we should wait for Zhongli?

dialogues.speaker: Zijiao
dialogues.text: That won't be necessary.

dialogues.speaker: Zijiao
dialogues.text: All things shall meet again in their time — for the waters know no rest, and the flowers their appointed season.

dialogues.speaker: Zijiao
dialogues.text: One need not fear that life is but a journey of goodbyes.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Is she... gone?

dialogues.speaker: Zhongli
dialogues.text: Yes, she's gone. A Deadly Self is formed from the body's impure vapors — so naturally, it cannot survive long in this world. Had it not been sustained by the remnant of Zibai's soul, it would have faded away a long time past.

dialogues.speaker: Zhongli
dialogues.text: Now that the remnant is gone, it has severed its ties to the mortal world.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Zhongli! When did you get here?

dialogues.speaker: Zhongli
dialogues.text: A while ago.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Paimon would've thought you'd at least wanna say goodbye...

dialogues.speaker: Zhongli
dialogues.text: Though mountains endure, the ceaseless waters will, at last, wear away their sharp edges. Thus must I meet the marks wrought upon her by the Ruler of Time with great caution.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Actually, you're just terrible at saying goodbye.

dialogues.speaker: Zhongli
dialogues.text: It may be goodbye for now, but someday, we will meet again.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Really? And when might that be?

dialogues.speaker: Zhongli
dialogues.text: Who can say for sure? Years and years from now, perhaps...

dialogues.speaker: Zhongli
dialogues.text: ...Or maybe tonight, at the Lantern Rite.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Are you saying... that if the White Horse Adeptus were to be resurrected, she'd still have the memories of the Three Deadly Selves? That she'd still remember us?

dialogues.speaker: Zhongli
dialogues.text: We will find out soon enough.

dialogues.speaker: Zhongli
dialogues.text: It is time. The Rite is about to begin.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Did we do it!? Do we finally get to meet the real White Horse Adeptus?
This place... Where am I?

dialogues.speaker: Zhongli
dialogues.text: A familiar land, now known by the name of Liyue.
"Liyue"? The peaks adorn... the clouded moon...
Then... Who might you be?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh no! She seems to have lost all her memories, after all...
And those countless lights in the sky... What are they?

dialogues.speaker: Zhongli
dialogues.text: These lights, each like a dwelling in glad accord, usher in this day of joyous rebirth.
And whose rebirth might that be?

dialogues.speaker: Zhongli
dialogues.text: That of my old friend, Zibai.
...Zibai?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Yeah, that's you! Don't you remember anything at all?
That's... me?

dialogues.speaker: Zibai
dialogues.text: Oh, yes... the Envoy of the Lunar Palace. My name... is Zibai indeed.

dialogues.speaker: Zibai
dialogues.text: Then... You must be...

dialogues.speaker: Zibai
dialogues.text: ...The Lord of Geo, Heaven's Star.

dialogues.speaker: Zhongli
dialogues.text: Many years have passed since we last saw one another. Zibai, my friend, welcome home.

dialogues.speaker: Zibai
dialogues.text: "Home"...?

dialogues.speaker: Zibai
dialogues.text: But why does this place... this "Liyue"... feel at once so strange, and yet so familiar?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Do you remember who we are?

dialogues.speaker: Zibai
dialogues.text: Who you are? Hmm, who are you... Ah, yes, I remember now.

dialogues.speaker: Zibai
dialogues.text: #You are that {M#young Wushou dancer, the one who seeks disciples}{F#treasure-hunting damsel, the one stricken by the poisonous fish stew}.

dialogues.speaker: Zibai
dialogues.text: #{M#How fares your quest for disciples? It must have yielded a truly prolific body of students by now, I trust?}{F#How goes your quest for treasure? You must have achieved both fame and fortune by now, I trust?}

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #Hey, you've got it all wrong! {M#You're talking about Gaming...}{F#You're talking about Lu Xiangxiang, and how many times do we have to tell you — she wasn't poisoned! Sheesh...}

dialogues.speaker: Zibai
dialogues.text: Hmm? But I could have sworn... Oh, that's right! You're that impudent blond youngster who kept meddling in my affairs!

dialogues.speaker: Zibai
dialogues.text: And to think, you even had the audacity to presume yourselves worthy of being... What was it again...

dialogues.speaker: Zibai
dialogues.text: ...Ah yes, of being my guides!

dialogues.speaker: Zibai
dialogues.text: How very wonderful to see you again, my most faithful and beloved guides! I trust all has been well in my absence?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Uhh... Well, she finally got it right, but that sudden mood swing felt even weirder... It's like her head's packed full of Slimes!

dialogues.speaker: Zhongli
dialogues.text: It is possible that her Selves have not yet settled — after all, they've only just been brought back together. It may be some time before she fully recovers.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh? You mean... kinda like she's still half-asleep?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: So, how long will it take for her to fully recover?

dialogues.speaker: Zhongli
dialogues.text: That, I cannot say for certain. Perhaps a few days, perhaps a few years.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: A few years!?

dialogues.speaker: Zhongli
dialogues.text: Mortal years are but a poor measure when divine beings tread the realm of dreams.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Well, if you say so... Anyway, at least she's whole again, right? That already seems like a pretty good outcome to Paimon.

dialogues.speaker: Zhongli
dialogues.text: Yes... There is little cause for worry. We need only wait and let time take its course.

dialogues.speaker: Zibai
dialogues.text: Say, what are those little creatures over there up to?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Celebrating Lantern Rite, of course! And those lights up in the sky, those are all Xiao Lanterns. This year, each and every one of them carries a little wish inside.

dialogues.speaker: Zibai
dialogues.text: "Lantern Rite," hmm...? Then... may I join in too?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Of course! Why else do you think we've been running around like headless chickens these past few days?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #Tell you what — {NICKNAME}, why don't we take the White Horse Adeptus out to celebrate?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Who knows, maybe seeing some familiar faces might help her find her feet?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Let's do that.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hey Zhongli — you've got some time on your hands now, right? Why don't you come along with us?

dialogues.speaker: Zhongli
dialogues.text: By no means a bad idea, Paimon.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh, and Zibai, before Paimon forgets — when we meet the others later, remember to wish them a "Happy Lantern Rite"!

dialogues.speaker: Zibai
dialogues.text: Happy... Lantern Rite?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Happy Lantern Rite!

dialogues.speaker: Zibai
dialogues.text: Yes... Happy Lantern Rite indeed.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hehe! Well then, let's go!

dialogues.speaker: Zhongli
dialogues.text: Lantern Rite... A night of joy, reunion, and moonlit blessings for all.
